name: Dijon
label: R&R / Warner
lede: Dijon Duenas grew up on military bases, cut his first records with a college friend in Maryland, and spent years as a name in other people's credits. Then he made an album for his newborn son, and Pitchfork put it at No. 2 for 2025.

eras.title: Ellicott City, a laptop and a friend named Abhi
eras.text: Duenas moved around enough that Maryland ended up as the place he lived longest. There he made hazy R&B with Abhirath Raju while finishing an English degree, and he learned production and singing by doing both.

years.src: The Fader: Dijon is imagining · SSENSE · The Washington Post · Wikipedia: Dijon Duenas
years.h: Dijon Duenas graduates with an English degree and a duo
years.p: He and high school friend Abhirath Raju put out a compilation and two EPs of washed-out R&B between 2012 and 2016, as Abhi//Dijon.
years.xp:
The Fader reported in 2018 that Duenas, a military kid shuttled between the U.S. and Germany, made his first beats on a four-track and FL Studio and only got serious about music in his last year at Maryland. SSENSE reports he first worked in Baltimore's DIY and punk circles before the R&B duo.

Duenas later told The Washington Post: "I moved around so much that Maryland is the place that I lived in longest, but I still had a mentality of a distance from the music scene there." Wikipedia lists the releases as the self-titled EP (2014), Stay Up (2015) and Montana (2016).

years.src: The Fader: Dijon is imagining · Wikipedia: Dijon Duenas · Dazed
years.h: Duenas and Raju move west, and the duo ends without a talk
years.p: Duenas on how Abhi//Dijon ended after the summer 2016 move from Ellicott City to Los Angeles, as told to The Fader. That year the pair were also credited on Nao's "Adore You".
years.xp:
"Once we got to Los Angeles, it just happened organically and naturally. It was pretty unspoken," Duenas told The Fader. Wikipedia says the two disbanded amicably.

Dazed lists the Nao credit as the first of several places his work was hiding in other people's records.

eras.title: The name in everyone else's credits
eras.text: He's solo now, but mostly heard through other people: backing vocals on a Brockhampton record, synths on a quarantine pop album, and two EPs that few outside Los Angeles had found yet.

years.h: A first solo single, and a backing vocal on Brockhampton's Saturation II
years.p: "Stranger" came out in 2017, the same year Duenas sang backing vocals on [[Brockhampton|3ac96b4c-4f42-48c8-b793-84dbf54d7ac6]]'s "Summer".
years.xp:
He kept going back. Duenas returned for songwriting and additional vocals on "1998 Truman" in 2018, and i-D's 2021 profile of him ran with photographs by the group's Kevin Abstract.

Dazed counts "Summer" as one of the first spots where listeners heard him without knowing it.

years.h: A quarantine album by [[Charli XCX|260b6184-8828-48eb-945c-bc4cb6fc34ca]], with Duenas in the credits
years.p: He and [[A. G. Cook|b12ef43e-72ad-43d0-b216-a8cd32f78852]] share work on "Pink Diamond" from How I'm Feeling Now; Duenas is credited on production, songwriting, synthesizer and drum programming.
years.xp:
That same month Duenas put out his own EP, How Do You Feel About Getting Married?, on Dark Green, R&R and Warner, following Sci Fi 1 (March 1, 2019).

NME describes the 2020 EP as the point where his self-imposed isolation gave way and friends started contributing.

eras.title: A guest-room record that travels
eras.text: Absolutely arrives with a co-producer who becomes his closest ally, a short film and a late-night slot. By summer 2022 it's on Barack Obama's playlist.

q: The process was very simple; Mike played drums, I played a weird backup thing.
years.src: Wikipedia: Absolutely · NME · i-D · The Fader: Dijon on spontaneity · SSENSE
years.p: Duenas and Michael Gordon (Mk.gee) co-produced the debut album at Duenas's Los Angeles home and in upstate New York. Pitchfork scored it 7.2, and The Fader ranked it No. 3 of 2021.
years.xp:
"Many Times" led on September 17, 2021, then "Rodeo Clown" on October 22. NME says the first single came from Gordon's drums: "It was very immediate what was supposed to be achieved based on Mike's drums," Duenas said. i-D reported the crew used a single fixed microphone to catch the whole room, laughter and TV static included, and let first-time songwriter Noah Le Gros sing lead on "Noah's Highlight Reel."

A short film companion followed December 22, 2021. In summer 2022 Barack Obama put "Many Times" on his playlist, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dijon Duenas · Wikipedia: Absolutely · The Washington Post
yt: Big Mike's on The Tonight Show
years.p: His network TV debut, less than three months after Absolutely came out.
years.xp:
That spring he opened two Bon Iver shows, in Mesa, Arizona and Austin, Texas, with a live band of Jack Karaszewski, Henry Kwapis, Mk.gee and Ryan Richter. He then headlined his own North American tour.

"The major philosophy that runs through the live show is that we get pretty bored just trying to tell the same story," he told The Washington Post.

eras.title: From the call-back list to his own record
eras.text: Between albums, other artists start calling Duenas. Then he finishes Baby, and the part-time credit becomes the best-reviewed R&B record of the year.

years.h: Duenas is in the credits of Mk.gee's Two Star & the Dream Police
years.p: Writer and producer on the February 9 release on R&R, the record that made Mk.gee a critical name.
years.xp: Dazed's rundown of Duenas's hidden credits also lists production on Matt Champion's "Slow Motion" featuring Jennie, and vocals on "Aphid" from Champion's Mika's Laundry, both from 2024.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dijon Duenas · Dazed · Stereogum: Dijon Sings
years.h: [[Justin Bieber|e0140a67-e4d1-4f13-8a01-364355bee46e]] puts Duenas on four songs of Swag
years.p: Duenas co-writes and produces. "Daisies", which he made with Mk.gee, reached No. 2 on the Hot 100.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Duenas also performs on "Devotion" and produced and co-wrote "Yukon", which reached No. 17. Stereogum reports he played "Yukon" live for the first time in Portland on November 1, 2025, and that Bieber had already shown up at one of his San Diego dates.

years.src: Exclaim! · Stereogum: Stream Dijon's Emotive · Wikipedia: Baby
years.h: Countdown clock for Baby comes with an asterisk
years.p: That was the caption on the clock Duenas posted a week ahead of release, with no singles out.
years.xp: Exclaim! reported the clock ran to midnight on August 14, with the album due the next day. Stereogum notes it arrived without advance singles. The samples cleared, and the album came out August 15.

years.src: Album of the Year · Wikipedia: Baby · Wikipedia: Dijon Duenas · The Fader: Review · Stereogum: Stream Dijon's Emotive · Dazed
years.h: Baby gets a 9.0 from Pitchfork and the No. 2 spot for 2025
years.p: Andrew Sarlo produced most of the 37 minutes, which are dedicated to Duenas's wife Joanie del Santo and their son.
years.xp:
Album of the Year's critic score list has Pitchfork at 90 and Paste at 100; Metacritic showed a 94 from seven reviews and Rolling Stone gave it 4.5 stars, per Wikipedia. Pitchfork's year-end list put it behind only Los Thuthanaka. Wikipedia lists Rolling Stone No. 4, Paste No. 5 and The Fader No. 13 on their year-end lists. Pitchfork is not fetchable from here, so the score is from Wikipedia and Album of the Year.

Beyond Sarlo and Mk.gee, credits include BJ Burton, Tommy King, Tobias Jesso Jr., Pino Palladino on bass and Justin Vernon on "Higher!", which also has Jenn Wasner of Baltimore's Wye Oak on bass. Vernon's Bon Iver had featured Duenas on "Day One" from Sable, Fable that April. The Fader described it as made at home, in isolation, with his family, and called the production "kitchen-sink maximalism." Dazed says the title comes from the son born in 2023.

years.h: Duenas turns up in Paul Thomas Anderson's One Battle After Another
years.p: Paul Thomas Anderson's film also stars Leonardo DiCaprio, Teyana Taylor and Alana Haim.
years.xp: Dazed and Primetimer both flagged the role as his first screen work. Wikipedia lists the film's release in September 2025.

years.src: The Baltimore Banner · Wikipedia: Grammy Award
years.h: Grammy nominations for Producer of the Year and Swag
years.p: Producer of the Year, Non-Classical, and Album of the Year. Both come from his work on other people's records, not Baby.
years.xp: The Baltimore Banner reported both nominations. At the February 2026 ceremony Cirkut won the producer award, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Dijon on Saturday Night Live, December 6, 2025
years.src: The Baltimore Banner · Rolling Stone · Primetimer
years.p: Melissa McCarthy hosted. Duenas had played a sold-out Fillmore Silver Spring show the night before, close to his old Maryland stomping grounds.
years.xp: The Baltimore Banner tied the appearance to his Ellicott City roots: he attended Centennial High School before Maryland. The Fillmore Silver Spring show on December 5 was sold out.

eras.title: A desert stage, filmed like a concert movie
eras.text: The Baby cycle reaches Coachella with a band set up like a jam session and cameras on stage.

years.cap: Dijon on guitar at Coachella, Indio, April 2026
years.h: Coachella gets eight musicians in a horseshoe
years.p: Paste compared the set to Stop Making Sense. Mk.gee played distorted guitar and Jack Karaszewski mixed live.
years.xp:
Paste puts the set on April 10 at 6:40 p.m., weekend one. The walkout used a pitched-up recording of the Family Guy theme, and the band built each song from scratch with cameras on stage. The stream stayed up only until 4 p.m. on April 11.

Setlist.fm lists a second weekend set on April 17.
